expected_no_table_zones.location: right-floated sidebar near top of article
expected_no_table_zones.looks_like: a bordered data table (has <table> tag, border/background styling, spans multiple rows)
expected_no_table_zones.reason: This is a MediaWiki 'vertical-navbox' template (class='vertical-navbox nowraplinks hlist') -- a topic-navigation sidebar (e.g. links to related Artificial Intelligence articles), not tabular data. It uses <table> purely as a CSS layout container, a very common real-world MediaWiki pattern.

expected_no_table_zones.location: small box near References/External links section
expected_no_table_zones.reason: This is the MediaWiki 'sistersitebox' template (role='presentation', class='mbox-small plainlinks sistersitebox') linking to Wikimedia Commons/Wikidata -- explicitly marked role='presentation' in the HTML itself, meaning even the source acknowledges this is NOT semantic tabular data, just layout.

expected_no_table_zones.location: bottom of article, before final closing tags
expected_no_table_zones.reason: This is a MediaWiki bottom navbox template (class='nowraplinks hlist navbox-inner') linking to related topic articles in a grid -- again a navigation/UI table, not data.

expected_noise_elements:
129 'mw-editsection' spans (the '[edit]' links MediaWiki injects into every heading) -- each is a SIBLING of the mw-headline span WITHIN THE SAME

/

tag, e.g.

History[edit]

. A naive '.textContent of h2' extraction will produce contaminated heading text like 'History[edit]' rather than clean 'History' -- this is the core, concrete mechanism behind named weak spot #1, not just an abstract concern.

MediaWiki table-of-contents block near the top (id='mw-toc-heading') -- a self-referential list of the very same headings, which could be double-counted as content if not recognized as TOC chrome. NOTE: this ToC block itself is wrapped in an <h2 id='mw-toc-heading'> tag reading 'Contents' -- this is a REAL 13th h2 tag in the raw markup (independently re-verified: 13 h2 + 31 h3 = 44 total heading tags, not 12+31=43 as an earlier draft of this rubric stated), but it is TOC/navigation chrome, not an article section heading, so it is deliberately excluded from the expected_headings list above even though Pith will genuinely encounter it in the markup.
notes_for_implementer: Concrete, verified mechanism for weak spot #1: every real article heading in this document IS wrapped in a real semantic <h2>/<h3> tag (13 h2 + 31 h3 = 44 total heading tags in the raw markup, one of which is the 'Contents' ToC heading rather than an article section -- corrected after independent re-verification found an earlier draft undercounted h2 as 12; the 43 mw-headline spans match 44 heading tags minus the 1 ToC heading, which has no mw-headline span of its own), so a tag-based heading detector alone should actually succeed at finding headings -- the failure mode is specifically in HEADING TEXT EXTRACTION: naive '.textContent' or similar on the h2/h3 element will include the sibling '[edit]' mw-editsection text, contaminating every single heading's extracted text. The correct behavior is to extract text ONLY from the '.mw-headline' span (or equivalent), not the whole h2/h3. Verify Pith's output headings read as clean 'History', 'Alan Turing', etc., NOT 'History[edit]' or similar. Separately, the 3 <table> elements in this document are 100% chrome/navigation, not data -- Pith must report zero tables for this document; any table reported is a false positive of exactly the kind named as weak spot #2.
